::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Let $R$ be a relation. Suppose that $A$ and $B$ are two sets. Then $R[A] \setminus R[B]$ $\subseteq$ $R[A\setminus B]$](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/3568453/let-r-be-a-relation-suppose-that-a-and-b-are-two-sets-then-ra-setmin), asked by [Abigail Webb](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/756496/abigail-webb) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2020-03-03; [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)):

> I know how to prove something is a subset of another but I’m not sure how to use the properties of the image to prove $x$ is not in the image of $B.$
:::

Assuming that Graham's clarification is correct, the left-hand side $R[A] \setminus R[B]$ is the set of all $x$ such that $x \mathrel{R} y$ for some $y$ in $A$, but $x \mathrel{R} z$ is true for no $z \in B$.

The right-hand side $R[A\setminus B]$ is the set of all $x$ such that $x \mathrel{R} y$ for some $y$ that is in $A$ but not in $B$.

Can you take it from there?
